A1.justification: Both PDFs describe SANSA, with matching authors, core methodology and experiments. Text, equations, tables, figures and appendices are readable, allowing retained content to be matched across restructuring and renumbering.

before.justification: V1 reports original SANSA benchmark results, ablations, feature analyses, linear probing and annotation-efficiency experiments.

after.justification: V2 retains original SANSA experiments and reports additional comparator controls, robustness tests, ablations and negative-prompt results.

M1.justification: The core frozen-SAM2 adapter pipeline, sequential training objective and segmentation losses remain. Appendix F adds exploratory semantic-negative extensions: inserting a negative reference with an empty mask into memory, or mapping negative-object features through an MLP into a learned negative token.

E1.justification: The existing object and part segmentation benchmarks remain. V2 adds Pascal-5i and COCO-to-Pascal transfer, DAVIS video and flipped-frame conditions, and independent TSS image pairs. Negative-prompt experiments also introduce target-image corrections and additional contrastive references, substantially broadening evaluated scenarios.

E2.justification: Table 1 removes HSNet and VAT from the original benchmark comparison and adds HMNet; HSNet and VAT appear in the new Pascal comparison. V2 also evaluates AENet, PMNet and MONA, and introduces SAM2-based versions of PerSAM, Matcher, VRP-SAM and GF-SAM in Table 7.

E3.justification: Generalist model size is revised from 234M to 250M parameters, with larger adapters reported. New experiments introduce class-disjoint cross-dataset evaluation, spatial-coherence measurements under controlled flips, and varying negative-click counts. Training prose changes Adam to AdamW, although Table 13 still says Adam; this establishes a documentation revision, not that experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: V2 retains the existing PCA, linear-probing, fine-tuning and tracker-transfer analyses while adding substantial controls: SAM-to-SAM2 substitutions, training from scratch, full-model fine-tuning, MONA, adapter placement and encoder scale. The training-objective ablation expands into sequence-length sensitivity. New analyses examine part correspondences, cross-dataset robustness, negative prompts and spatial continuity.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, significance tests or uncertainty bars. Additional averages and result rows in v2 do not introduce a new uncertainty-reporting practice.

E6.justification: Table 1 replaces SANSA's LVIS 1-/5-shot scores of 49.8/55.9 with 48.8/53.9, and COCO scores of 60.1/67.3 with 60.2/64.3. COCO 5-shot consequently falls below GF-SAM's unchanged 66.8. Table 2 also revises results while reporting a larger generalist model. Numerous new entries cover comparator upgrades, ablations, transfer, negative prompts and spatial coherence; these are not evidence of uniform same-setting improvement.

T1.justification: The pseudo-video, memory-attention, adapter and training-sequence equations retain their mathematical substance despite reordered presentation and revised indices. Neither version supplies formal theorems or proofs. The added spatial-coherence evaluation uses an existing metric rather than introducing new theory.

C1.justification: The first contribution removes the FSS-specific qualifier from its claim to first investigate SAM2's semantic structure. Headline performance margins are revised, including the LVIS advantage from 9.3 to 8.3 points. The central claims about latent semantics, unified segmentation, flexible prompting and efficiency remain.

C2.justification: V2 explains spatial continuity as a bias learned during pretraining rather than an architectural constraint, and expands the interpretation of adapter capacity and nonlinearity. It explicitly qualifies semantic-negative prompting as exploratory because standardized protocols and baselines are lacking. The existing limitations in Appendix A.1 remain essentially unchanged.

D1.justification: Compared with v1's brief implementation description, Appendix H discloses adapted layers, channel-dependent hidden widths, loss weights, gradient clipping, batch size 32 and eight A100 GPUs. V2 also specifies training sequence length, independent-target inference and prompt generation. Disclosure improves substantially, but Table 13 conflicts with the prose on Adam versus AdamW and approximately 20M versus 25M generalist trainable parameters.

R1.justification: Related work adds an explicit contrast between diffusion's spatial precision and DINOv2's semantic strengths, positioning SAM2 as combining both. New citations cover SAMwise, MONA, additional comparators, datasets and protocols; Appendix H adds in-context learning background. The central research positioning remains intact.

P1.justification: V2 reorganizes the method exposition to define the task first, separates domain/style generalization from ablations, and replaces the short ablation discussion with three explanatory questions. The appendices are reorganized and gain a roadmap and extensive explanations of evaluation conventions. Terminology is revised throughout, particularly from zero-shot to frozen or training-free.

P2.justification: Figure 3 is substantially redrawn, Figure 4 gains a correspondence panel, and Table 3 consolidates and restructures ablations. Domain-shift and part-segmentation galleries expand, a prompt gallery is added, and new tables display the additional experiments and hyperparameters. Existing PCA, probing and qualitative comparisons are retained or relocated rather than newly introduced.

improvement.justification: V2 addresses important gaps with SAM2 comparator controls, targeted adaptation ablations, and controlled spatial-continuity and cross-dataset tests, strengthening evidence for SANSA's mechanism and generalization. The implementation and prompt-generation details substantially improve transparency. These benefits outweigh localized reporting flaws, including optimizer and parameter-count conflicts, unreconciled LVIS scores in Tables 1 and 9, and inconsistent fold means in Table 10.
